THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 2 are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 447, 468, 471 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, petitioners- accused herein by fabricating the documents purported to establish that the subject property belongs to them criminally trespassed into the subject property, abused the complainant in a filthy language and also threatened her with dire consequences.

3. The parties are present before this Court with their respective counsels, and have filed an application under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for compounding of the offences,
stating that, the parties have instituted a suit in NC: 2023:KHC:29405 O.S.No.5880/2022 against the mother of the complainant and in the said suit, the parties have amicably settled the dispute Smt. Geetha H Singh vs State By Amruthahalli Police Station on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153998715/
2 among themselves and the petitioner No.2 has agreed to give up his claim over the subject property subject to receipt of a sum of Rs.20 Lakh.
4.

entities.text: Geetha H Singh vs State By Amruthahalli Police Station
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though the offences alleged against the petitioners- accused herein are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves and the respondent No.2 having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings against the petitioners-accused herein the probability of conviction is remote and bleak.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.8190/2023 on the file of the VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stands quashed.
